results.title: Frobenius and spectral norms: mixed inequalities
results.informal: Submultiplicativity: $\|AB\|_F \le \|A\|\,\|B\|_F$ and $\|AB\|_F \le \|A\|_F\,\|B\|$. Norm comparison: $\|A\| \le \|A\|_F \le \sqrt{\operatorname{rank}(A)}\,\|A\|$. Both norms are unitarily invariant, and $$\|A\|_F^2 = \operatorname{tr}(A^\top A) = \sum_i \sigma_i^2.$$

results.title: Singular value decomposition of a matrix
results.informal: Every $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ factors as $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)} \ge 0$. Splitting at rank $k$ gives the block form $$A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top.$$
results.conclusion: $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)} \ge 0$; at rank $k$, $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$

formalizations.note: IsSVD A U V: Uᵀ U = 1, Vᵀ V = 1, A = U · rectDiag (singularValues A) · Vᵀ, where singularValues A : ℕ → ℝ is Mathlib's LinearMap.singularValues of toEuclideanLin A (zero-indexed, antitone, zero beyond the rank). Also uniqueness of σ, block split at k (IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail), AᵀA and AAᵀ diagonalisations, frobSq = Σσ², invariance under orthogonal factors and transpose.

results.title: Eckart–Young–Mirsky: best rank-k approximation
results.informal: Both minima are attained by the truncated SVD $\lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k$: $$\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\| = \sigma_{k+1}(A), \qquad \min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2.$$
results.conclusion: $\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\| = \sigma_{k+1}(A)$ and $\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2$, both attained by $\lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k$
results.notes: The extension proves the Frobenius minimum, attained by its actual truncated SVD, for every target rank and shape. The spectral-norm minimum remains a separate open component; this combined entry is not promoted by the Frobenius proof.

results.title: Weyl and Mirsky perturbation bounds for singular values
results.informal: For every $i$, $|\sigma_i(A+E) - \sigma_i(A)| \le \|E\|$, and $$\Big(\sum_i \big(\sigma_i(A+E) - \sigma_i(A)\big)^2\Big)^{1/2} \le \|E\|_F.$$

results.title: Courant–Fischer min-max and Rayleigh quotients
results.informal: For Hermitian $A$, $$\lambda_k(A) = \max_{\dim S = k}\ \min_{x \in S,\ \|x\|=1} x^\top A x.$$ In particular $\lambda_{\max}$ is the sup of the Rayleigh quotient and $\lambda_{\min}$ the inf.
results.conclusion: $\lambda_k(A) = \max_{\dim S = k}\ \min_{x \in S,\ \|x\|=1} x^\top A x$; in particular $\lambda_{\max} = \sup_{\|x\|=1} x^\top Ax$ and $\lambda_{\min} = \inf_{\|x\|=1} x^\top Ax$

results.notes: The user's definitions lambdaMax/lambdaMin (Tropp) and lamMin (LRA) are both the Rayleigh form; the full min-max is what interlacing and Weyl need.

results.title: Cauchy interlacing for principal submatrices and compressions
results.informal: If $Q$ has $k$ orthonormal columns then $$\lambda_{i+n-k}(A) \le \lambda_i(Q^\top A Q) \le \lambda_i(A).$$ Used for Nyström, Lanczos/Ritz values and column subset selection.

results.title: Rank: products, sums, and rank-k matrices
results.informal: $\operatorname{rank}(AB) \le \min(\operatorname{rank} A, \operatorname{rank} B)$; $\operatorname{rank}(A+B) \le \operatorname{rank} A + \operatorname{rank} B$; $\operatorname{rank}(QX) = \operatorname{rank} X$ for $Q$ with orthonormal columns.
results.conclusion: $\operatorname{rank}(AB) \le \min(\operatorname{rank} A, \operatorname{rank} B)$, $\operatorname{rank}(A+B) \le \operatorname{rank} A + \operatorname{rank} B$ and $\operatorname{rank}(QX) = \operatorname{rank} X$

results.title: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse and its identities
results.informal: The general real Moore–Penrose inverse exists at every rank, is unique, and satisfies all four Penrose identities. It agrees with pinvL/pinvR when the respective Gram matrix is invertible. Its products are the orthogonal range projectors. Its norm is zero for the zero matrix and otherwise the reciprocal of the smallest positive singular value. For every A, $\|A^\dagger\|_F^2=\operatorname{tr}((AA^\top)^\dagger)$.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, over arbitrary finite index types
Full-column or full-row rank is required only for the ordinary inverse formulas
results.conclusion: $AA^\dagger A=A$, $A^\dagger AA^\dagger=A^\dagger$, $(AA^\dagger)^\top=AA^\dagger$, $(A^\dagger A)^\top=A^\dagger A$; the inverse is unique, and $\|A^\dagger\|=0$ when rank is zero, otherwise $1/\sigma_{\operatorname{rank}(A)}(A)$.

formalizations.note: Full-rank specialization; the general rank-deficient case is covered by moorePenroseInverse and its Penrose identities.

results.title: Loewner order and the continuous functional calculus on matrices
results.informal: $A \preceq B$ iff $B - A$ is PSD. Trace and conjugation are monotone. $f(A)$ for Hermitian $A$ is defined via the eigendecomposition, including $\sqrt{A}$, $\exp A$ and $\log A$.

results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - 2d\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/(cL))$, every eigenvalue of $\frac{1}{k}\sum_j x_jx_j^\top$ lies in $[1-\varepsilon, 1+\varepsilon]$
results.notes: Matrix Chernoff is proved; this packaging is cheap and unlocks SRHT, leverage-score sampling and sparsification.

results.title: Matrix Freedman / martingale Bernstein
results.informal: Martingale version of matrix Bernstein; used for adaptive sampling and streaming.

results.informal: Moment form of the matrix series bound; sharper for subspace embeddings.

results.title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma
results.informal: $n$ points embed into $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ dimensions with all pairwise distances preserved to within $1 \pm \varepsilon$; union bound over the distributional lemma.

results.title: Subspace embedding: definition and equivalent forms
results.informal: $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$ ($U$ orthonormal) iff $\|SUx\|^2 \in (1\pm\varepsilon)\|x\|^2$ for all $x$, iff $\sigma(SU) \subset [\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}, \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}]$, iff $\|U^\top S^\top SU - I\| \le \varepsilon$. results.title: Gaussian matrices are oblivious subspace embeddings
results.informal: $k^{-1/2}G$ with $k \ge C(d + \log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon^2$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for any fixed $d$-dimensional subspace with probability $1 - \delta$.
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$
results.notes: One line from the Mission III goal plus rotation invariance.

results.title: Subsampled randomized Hadamard transform is a subspace embedding
results.informal: SRHT with $k = O\big(\varepsilon^{-2}(d + \log n)\log d\big)$ rows is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding. Proof: row flattening by random signs, then matrix Chernoff sampling.

results.conclusion: with high probability, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$

results.title: Sparse oblivious subspace embeddings (CountSketch, OSNAP, SparseStack)
results.informal: CountSketch with $k = O(d^2/\varepsilon^2)$ rows is an OSE; OSNAP/SparseStack with $O(d/\varepsilon^2)$ rows and few nonzeros per column.

results.conclusion: with constant probability, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$

results.title: Approximate matrix multiplication by row sampling
results.informal: Sampling $c$ column/row pairs with probabilities $p_i \propto \|A_{:,i}\|\,\|B_{i,:}\|$ gives $$\mathbb{E}\|AB - CR\|_F^2 \le \frac{\|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2}{c}.$$
hypotheses: $C$, $R$ the sampled columns of $A$ and rows of $B$, rescaled by $1/\sqrt{c\,p_i}$

results.title: Approximate multiplication from a subspace embedding
results.informal: If $S$ satisfies the JL moment property then $$\mathbb{E}\|A^\top S^\top SB - A^\top B\|_F^2 \le \varepsilon^2\|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2.$$ The glue between embeddings and least squares.
hypotheses: $S$ satisfies the JL moment property with parameter $\varepsilon$

results.title: Leverage scores: definition and basic properties
aliases: row norms of an orthonormal basis

results.title: Leverage-score row sampling is a subspace embedding
results.informal: Sampling $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}d\log(d/\delta))$ rows with $p_i \propto \ell_i$ and rescaling gives an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding with probability $1 - \delta$. The same theorem gives spectral sparsification.
hypotheses: $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}d\log(d/\delta))$ rows sampled i.i.d. with $p_i \propto \ell_i$ and rescaled by $1/\sqrt{kp_i}$
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the sampling matrix $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(A)$

results.title: Volume sampling and column subset selection
results.informal: Sampling $k$ columns with probability proportional to squared volume gives $$\mathbb{E}\|A - \pi_S(A)\|_F^2 \le (k+1)\,\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2.$$
hypotheses: a set $S$ of $k$ columns sampled with probability proportional to $\det(A_S^\top A_S)$
$\pi_S$ the orthogonal projection onto the span of the chosen columns

results.informal: For PSD $A$ and any $\Omega$: $A \succeq A\langle\Omega\rangle := A\Omega(\Omega^\top A\Omega)^\dagger\Omega^\top A \succeq 0$, and $A - A\langle\Omega\rangle$ is the Schur complement. results.conclusion: $0 \preceq A\langle\Omega\rangle \preceq A$, $A - A\langle\Omega\rangle$ is a Schur complement, and $\|A - A\langle\Omega\rangle\| \le \|(I-P)A^{1/2}\|^2$

formalizations.usage: From `ha : 0 < a`, `hab : a < b`, `hp : p.degree ≤ q`, `hp0 : p.eval 0 = 1`, `hb : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, |p.eval x| ≤ M`; gives `1 / (T ℝ q).eval ((b + a)/(b - a)) ≤ M`.
Pass `q`, `ha`, `hab`; gives `IsLeast {M | ∃ p, p.degree ≤ q ∧ p.eval 0 = 1 ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, |p.eval x| ≤ M} (1 / (T ℝ q).eval ((b+a)/(b-a)))`.
From `ha`, `hab`, `hx : x ∈ Icc a b`; gives `|(chebyshevResidual a b q).eval x| ≤ 1 / (T ℝ q).eval ((b+a)/(b-a))`.
From `q`, `ha`, `hab`, `hx : x ∈ Icc a b`; gives `|(chebyshevResidual a b q).eval x| ≤ 2 * ((√b - √a)/(√b + √a))^q` (the CG rate).
From `ha`, `hab`; gives `(chebyshevResidual a b q).eval 0 = 1`.
`(chebyshevResidual a b q).degree ≤ q`, no hypotheses.

results.title: Monic Chebyshev polynomial has the smallest sup norm
aliases: 2^{1-q} T_q is the smallest monic polynomial
results.informal: Every monic $p$ of degree $q \ge 1$ has $\max_{[-1,1]}|p| \ge 2^{1-q}$, attained by $2^{1-q}T_q$. The reason Chebyshev nodes are the right interpolation points.

formalizations.usage: From `hp : p.Monic`, `hdeg : p.natDegree = q`, `hb : ∀ x ∈ Icc (-1) 1, |p.eval x| ≤ M`; gives `1 / 2^(q-1) ≤ M` (also for `q = 0`).
`IsLeast {M | ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc (-1) 1, |p.eval x| ≤ M} (1 / 2^(q-1))`.
`(C (1 / 2^(q-1)) * T ℝ q).Monic`; with `natDegree_inv_two_pow_mul_T` and `abs_eval_inv_two_pow_mul_T_le` the attaining polynomial.

results.title: Gap-amplifying Chebyshev polynomial
results.informal: $p(x) = T_q(x/\alpha)/T_q(1+\gamma)$ has $p(\alpha(1+\gamma)) = 1$, $p \ge 1$ beyond, and $|p| \le 2(1+\sqrt{2\gamma})^{-q}$ on $[-\alpha,\alpha]$: degree $O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\sqrt\gamma)$ separates a gap $\gamma$ (gap-independent version: $\gamma = \varepsilon$).

formalizations.usage: Pass `q`, `hα : 0 < α`, `hγ : 0 ≤ γ`, `hx : x ∈ Icc (-α) α`; gives `|(chebyshevAmplifier α γ q).eval x| ≤ 2 / (1 + √(2γ))^q`.
Pass `q`, `hα`, `hγ`, `hx : α * (1 + γ) ≤ x`; gives `1 ≤ (chebyshevAmplifier α γ q).eval x`.
Pass `q`, `hα`, `hγ`; gives `(chebyshevAmplifier α γ q).eval (α * (1 + γ)) = 1`.
`(chebyshevAmplifier α γ q).degree ≤ q`.

results.title: Polynomial approximation of 1/x on [a,b]
results.informal: There is $p$ of degree $< q$ with $|p(x) - 1/x| \le \tfrac{2}{a}\big(\tfrac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^q$ on $[a,b]$: the polynomial behind the CG and Lanczos-solve $\sqrt\kappa$ rates.
results.conclusion: $\exists p$ with $\deg p < q$ and $|p(x) - 1/x| \le \tfrac{2}{a}\big(\tfrac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^q$ for all $x \in [a,b]$

formalizations.usage: Pass `q`, `ha : 0 < a`, `hab : a < b`; gives `∃ p : ℝ[X], p.degree < q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, |p.eval x - 1/x| ≤ (2/a) * ((√b - √a)/(√b + √a))^q`.

results.title: Markov brothers' inequality
results.informal: If $\deg p \le q$ then $\max_{[-1,1]}|p'| \le q^2\max_{[-1,1]}|p|$ (sharp for $T_q$); on $[a,b]$ the constant is $2q^2/(b-a)$. Not to be confused with Markov's probability inequality.

formalizations.usage: From `hp : p.degree ≤ q`, `hb : ∀ y ∈ Icc (-1) 1, |p.eval y| ≤ M`, `hx : x ∈ Icc (-1) 1`; gives `|(derivative p).eval x| ≤ q^2 * M`.
formalizations.note: sharp constant; equality case not formalised

formalizations.usage: Interval form: from `hab : a < b`, `hp`, `hb : ∀ y ∈ Icc a b, |p.eval y| ≤ M`, `hx : x ∈ Icc a b`; gives `|(derivative p).eval x| ≤ 2 * q^2 / (b - a) * M`.

results.title: Bernstein's inequality for polynomials
results.informal: If $\deg p \le q$ and $|p| \le M$ on $[-1,1]$ then $|p'(x)| \le qM/\sqrt{1-x^2}$ for $|x| < 1$. The interior half of the Markov brothers' inequality.

formalizations.usage: From `hp : p.degree ≤ q`, `hb : ∀ y ∈ Icc (-1) 1, |p.eval y| ≤ M`, `hx : |x| < 1`; gives `|(derivative p).eval x| ≤ q * M / √(1 - x^2)`.
formalizations.note: proved algebraically via a Hasse-derivative odd part, no trigonometric polynomials

results.title: Lagrange interpolation: existence, uniqueness, basis
results.informal: Through $q+1$ distinct nodes there is exactly one polynomial of degree $\le q$ with prescribed values, $L = \sum_i f(x_i)\ell_i$ with $\ell_i = \prod_{j\ne i}\frac{x-x_j}{x_i-x_j}$. All in Mathlib.
results.conclusion: $L = \sum_i f_i\ell_i$ is the unique polynomial of degree $\le q$ with $L(x_i) = f_i$; the nodal polynomial is $\omega(x) = \prod_i (x - x_i)$

formalizations.usage: `interpolate s v r : F[X]`, the polynomial of degree `< #s` with value `r i` at node `v i`.
From `hvs : Set.InjOn v s`, `hi : i ∈ s`; gives `(interpolate s v r).eval (v i) = r i`.
Uniqueness: a polynomial of degree `< #s` equals the interpolant of its own values.
`nodal s v = ∏ i ∈ s, (X - C (v i))`.

results.title: Lagrange interpolation remainder
results.informal: For $f \in C^{q+1}[a,b]$ and distinct nodes, $f(x) - L(x) = \frac{f^{(q+1)}(\xi)}{(q+1)!}\prod_i (x-x_i)$ for some $\xi \in [a,b]$. Proved by generalised Rolle.

formalizations.usage: From `hab : a < b`, nodes `v : Fin (q+1) → ℝ` injective with values in `Icc a b`, `hx : x ∈ Icc a b`, `hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)`, `hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Ioo a b)`; gives `∃ ξ ∈ Ioo a b, f x - (Lagrange.interpolate univ v (f ∘ v)).eval x = iteratedDeriv (q+1) f ξ / (q+1)! * (Lagrange.nodal univ v).eval x`.
formalizations.note: ξ in the open interval; derivatives are the global `iteratedDeriv`

formalizations.usage: Generalised Rolle: `q + 2` zeros of `f` at strictly increasing `v : Fin (q+2) → ℝ` in `Icc a b`, `f` continuous on `Icc a b`, `f^{(k)}` continuous on `Ioo a b` for `1 ≤ k ≤ q`; gives `∃ ξ ∈ Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q+1) f ξ = 0`.
Generalised Rolle with the zeros given as a `Finset` of card `q + 2`.

results.title: Chebyshev interpolation error
results.informal: Interpolating at the zeros of $T_{q+1}$ makes the nodal polynomial $2^{-q}T_{q+1}$, so $|f - L| \le \frac{\max|f^{(q+1)}|}{2^q (q+1)!}$ on $[-1,1]$.
hypotheses: $f$ is $(q+1)$ times differentiable on $[-1,1]$ with $|f^{(q+1)}| \le M$
$L$ the interpolant at the $q+1$ zeros of $T_{q+1}$

formalizations.usage: From `hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc (-1) 1)`, `hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Ioo (-1) 1)`, `hM : ∀ ξ ∈ Ioo (-1) 1, |iteratedDeriv (q+1) f ξ| ≤ M`; gives `∀ x ∈ Icc (-1) 1, |f x - (Lagrange.interpolate univ (chebyshevZero (q+1)) (f ∘ chebyshevZero (q+1))).eval x| ≤ M / (2^q * (q+1)!)`.
`Lagrange.nodal univ (chebyshevZero q) = C (1 / 2^(q-1)) * T ℝ q`.
From `hx : x ∈ Icc (-1) 1`; gives `|(Lagrange.nodal univ (chebyshevZero q)).eval x| ≤ 1 / 2^(q-1)`.
`(T ℝ q).eval (chebyshevZero q k) = 0`.

results.title: Polynomial approximation of analytic functions (Bernstein ellipse)
results.informal: If $f$ is analytic in the Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ with $|f| \le M$ there, then $\min_{\deg p \le q}\max_{[-1,1]}|f - p| \le \frac{2M\rho^{-q}}{\rho - 1}$. What the SLQ and Lanczos-FA analyses cite for $\log$, $\exp$, $x^{-1/2}$.
hypotheses: $f$ analytic on the Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ ($\rho > 1$) with $|f| \le M$ there

results.title: Schur's inequality for polynomials of degree below q
results.informal: If $\deg r < q$ and $\sqrt{1-x^2}\,|r(x)| \le M$ on $[-1,1]$ then $|r| \le qM$ on $[-1,1]$. The step that turns Bernstein's interior bound into Markov's uniform bound.

formalizations.usage: From `hq : 0 < q`, `hr : r.degree < q`, `hb : ∀ y ∈ Icc (-1) 1, √(1 - y^2) * |r.eval y| ≤ M`, `hx : x ∈ Icc (-1) 1`; gives `|r.eval x| ≤ q * M`.

libraries.name: NLAlib (this repo)
libraries.scope: The library this atlas tracks. Layered modules Matrix → Concentration → Gaussian → Sketching → LowRank/Estimation/Krylov → Solvers. NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/ is Tropp 2015 Ch. 3–8 (formerly the standalone TroppMatrixConcentration project, all Proved on Prove2me), reorganised by topic: Laplace, Series, Chernoff, Bernstein, Intrinsic, OperatorConvexity, Defs. Gaussian/ holds the ported Gaussian Random Matrices series: Concentration/ (integration by parts, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, log-Sobolev, Herbst), Comparison/ (Slepian, Sudakov–Fernique, Gordon minimax), Extreme/ (Lipschitz, Gordon, Chevet, spectral second moment, chi-square, small ball, deviation), InverseMoments/ (inverse Wishart, pseudoinverse tails), Moments/ (fourth moment, approximate multiplication).

libraries.name: Mathlib
libraries.scope: Upstream. Has stdGaussian / multivariateGaussian, HasSubgaussianMGF and the Chernoff-method sum bound, LinearMap.singularValues, the scoped Loewner order on matrices with CFC, Schur complements, matrix exponential, Gamma distribution. Lacks matrix SVD factorization, Eckart–Young, Weyl, Moore–Penrose, chi-square tails, any random matrix theory.

libraries.name: Gaussian Random Matrices I–III (Prove2me)
libraries.scope: Three-mission series in namespace GaussianMatrix on Prove2me (73 accepted solutions). Fully ported into NLAlib/Gaussian/ on 2026-10-09. The Wishart eigenvalue density bound gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral was historically an unproved Prove2me statement; it is now completed locally by the unshifted operator route. Kept for provenance.

libraries.name: LRA (Chen–Persson formalization)
libraries.scope: Local project (~/Documents/Papers/LRA-paper/formal). 253 theorems; RSVD, GN, tGN, etRSVD, etGN proved conditional on explicit Gaussian Props in LRA/Standard/Gaussian.lean.

libraries.name: HighDimProb
libraries.scope: External. Hoeffding, Bernstein, Hanson–Wright with explicit constant 1/(256e²) stated on Mathlib's HasSubgaussianMGF and iIndepFun, covering numbers, Dudley chaining, a Matrix Bernstein route, sample covariance. Pinned to Lean v4.29.1 and reported failing to build on v4.31–v4.33, so it cannot be a lake dependency of the Prove2me-pinned projects; treat as a proof quarry to port from.

libraries.scope: External, ~30k lines. Gaussian Lipschitz concentration via Gaussian log-Sobolev; Dudley entropy integral.
